regions._about: Body-map regions. A region word adds its systems (weight 1) and the concerns people usually mean there (weight 1.5). Also the hotspots of the page's body map. 'with_pain': concerns promoted to full weight when the query also says pain or inflammation ("my head hurts" = headache).

expand._about: Concern or system -> actions that traditions use for it. The search adds these as weaker matches.

notes._about: Shown above results when the query touches this tag. Plain safety context, not diagnosis.
notes.urinary: Kidney problems change what is safe: many diuretic and high-potassium herbs (and licorice, noni, chaga, Aristolochia) are cautioned or dangerous with kidney disease. Swelling in the feet or legs can come from the kidneys, the heart or the veins.
notes.cardiovascular: Heart and blood-pressure medicines interact with many herbs (hawthorn, licorice, St John's wort, ginseng, dan shen). Chest pain or breathlessness is an emergency.
notes.liver: Many supplements can harm the liver (green tea extract, kava, comfrey, he shou wu, turmeric extracts). Yellow skin or eyes are a warning sign.
notes.reproductive: Pregnancy, trying to conceive and breastfeeding change everything: read every card's pregnancy line.
notes.endocrine: Herbs that lower blood sugar can add to diabetes medicines and cause hypos; thyroid medicines interact with several herbs.
notes.mind: Herbs for mood can clash with antidepressants (St John's wort, ayahuasca, kanna, saffron). If you feel unsafe, the Step outside button has crisis lines.
notes.low-mood: If low mood is heavy or you have thoughts of harming yourself, the Step outside button has crisis lines that answer now.
notes.oedema: Sudden or one-sided swelling, or swelling with breathlessness, is a warning sign.
notes.blood-sugar: Herbs that lower blood sugar add to diabetes medicines and can drop it dangerously.
notes.infection: Fever with spreading redness is a warning sign; herbs and oils are not antibiotics.

red_flags._about: Phrases that make the search show the emergency panel (emergency numbers and the Step outside button) above results. Not a diagnosis.

caution_words._about: Words looked for in a card's contra and safety text when the query touches this system: a match puts a red 'cautioned' chip on the result.

Ayurveda.say: India's classical medicine, more than 2,000 years old. The name means 'knowledge of life'.

dosha.say: In Ayurveda, one of three body energies (vata, pitta, kapha). Everyone has a personal mix.

vata.say: In Ayurveda, the airy, moving energy: dry, cold, light, restless.

pitta.say: In Ayurveda, the fiery energy: heat, sharpness, digestion.

kapha.say: In Ayurveda, the earthy, watery energy: heavy, steady, moist.

agni.say: In Ayurveda, the 'digestive fire' that turns food into you.

ama.say: In Ayurveda, sticky, half-digested waste left when digestion is weak.

ojas.say: In Ayurveda, the refined essence of good health and vigour.

rasayana.say: In Ayurveda, a rejuvenating remedy or regimen for long life and strength.

vajikarana.say: The branch of Ayurveda about vitality, desire and fertility.

dinacharya.say: Ayurveda's daily routine: waking early, tongue scraping, oil massage and the rest.

ritucharya.say: Ayurveda's seasonal routine: changing diet and habits with the seasons.

abhyanga.say: Ayurvedic self-massage with warm oil, usually before a bath.

panchakarma.say: Ayurveda's deep cleanse: 'five actions', done over days in a clinic.

ghee.say: Clarified butter: butter simmered until only the golden fat is left.

ghrita.say: Ghee cooked with herbs, an Ayurvedic way to carry medicine.

taila.say: An Ayurvedic oil cooked with herbs, used for massage.

bhasma.say: An Ayurvedic ash made by purifying and burning metals or minerals.

Siddha.say: The traditional medicine of Tamil South India.

Unani.say: Greek medicine as carried into Arabic and Persian, still practised in South Asia.

sharbat.say: A sweet herbal syrup or cordial (the word behind 'syrup' and 'sherbet').

qi.say: In Chinese medicine, the life energy that flows through the body. Said 'chee'.

yin.say: In Chinese thought, the cool, dark, moist, resting side of everything.

yang.say: In Chinese thought, the warm, bright, dry, active side of everything.

shen.say: In Chinese medicine, the spirit or mind, said to live in the heart.

jing.say: In Chinese medicine, your deep inborn essence, stored in the 'kidneys'.

meridian.say: In Chinese medicine, a channel that qi flows along; acupuncture points sit on them.

damp.say: In Chinese medicine, a heavy, sluggish, boggy state in the body.

Kampo.say: Japan's own form of Chinese herbal medicine; 148 of its formulas are covered by Japan's national health insurance.

Sowa Rigpa.say: Tibetan medicine. The name means 'science of healing'.

decoction.say: Hard parts (roots, bark, seeds) simmered in water, then strained.

infusion.say: Leaves or flowers steeped in hot water, like tea.

tincture.say: Herbs soaked in alcohol for weeks, then strained.

tisane.say: Herbal tea made without the tea plant.

salve.say: A soft balm of herb-infused oil set with beeswax.

poultice.say: Mashed fresh herbs laid straight on the skin.

essential oil.say: The concentrated scent of a plant, usually steam-distilled. Strong stuff.

carrier oil.say: A plain oil (like almond or olive) used to dilute essential oils.

adaptogen.say: A herbalists' word for a plant said to help the body cope with stress.

nervine.say: A herbalists' word for a plant used to calm or steady the nerves.

carminative.say: Used to ease wind and bloating.

demulcent.say: Slippery and soothing: coats sore, irritated tissue.

expectorant.say: Loosens mucus so you can cough it up.

astringent.say: Tightens and dries tissue, like the pucker of strong tea.

emmenagogue.say: Used to bring on a period. Dangerous in pregnancy.

febrifuge.say: Used to bring down a fever.

vulnerary.say: Used on wounds to help them close.

rubefacient.say: A warming rub that makes the skin flush red.

alterative.say: Old herbalists' word for a 'blood cleanser'.

cholagogue.say: Gets bile flowing from the gallbladder.

mucilage.say: The slippery gel some plants make in water, like soaked flax or okra.

pyrrolizidine alkaloids.say: Plant chemicals (in comfrey, coltsfoot, borage) that can slowly destroy the liver.

phototoxic.say: Makes skin burn or blister in sunlight after contact.

coumarin.say: A sweet-smelling plant chemical; in large amounts it harms the liver and thins blood.

thujone.say: A chemical in wormwood, sage and cedar that can cause seizures in large amounts.

salicylates.say: Aspirin's natural relatives, found in willow bark and meadowsweet.

venik.say: A bundle of birch or oak twigs used to beat yourself in the banya.

bannik.say: The spirit who lives in the banya, behind the stove.

znakharka.say: A Slavic village healer ('one who knows').

zagovor.say: A Slavic healing charm, whispered over water, salt or the sick person.

curandera.say: A healer in Latin American folk medicine.

limpia.say: A spiritual cleansing: the body swept with herbs or an egg.

susto.say: In Latin American healing, 'fright sickness': part of the soul knocked loose by a shock.

mal de ojo.say: The evil eye, in Latin American tradition.

temazcal.say: A Mesoamerican sweat lodge of stone or adobe.

rongoā.say: Māori healing with plants, prayer and massage.

kahuna.say: A Hawaiian expert or priest, such as a master healer.

ngangkari.say: Traditional healers of the Central and Western Desert peoples of Australia.

sangoma.say: A Southern African diviner-healer who works with the ancestors.

muthi.say: Traditional medicine in Southern Africa (plants, minerals, animal parts).

ruqyah.say: Healing by reciting the Qur'an over a person or over water.

hijama.say: Wet cupping, recommended in Islamic Prophetic medicine.

Prophetic medicine.say: Healing advice gathered from the sayings of the Prophet Muhammad (al-Tibb al-Nabawi).

hadith.say: A recorded saying or act of the Prophet Muhammad.

EMA.say: The European Medicines Agency, which publishes reviews of herbal medicines.

Cochrane.say: A respected network that pools all the trials on a question and summarises them.

NCCIH.say: The US government's centre for research on complementary medicine.

CITES.say: The international treaty that controls trade in endangered plants and animals.

IUCN.say: The body that keeps the Red List of threatened species.

serotonin syndrome.say: A dangerous overload of the brain messenger serotonin: agitation, fever, shaking.

MAOI.say: A type of drug (or plant chemical) that blocks an enzyme; it reacts badly with many medicines and foods.

CYP3A4.say: A liver and gut enzyme that breaks down about half of all medicines.

anticoagulant.say: A blood thinner, such as warfarin.

placebo.say: A dummy treatment used in trials to compare against the real thing.

succussion.say: In homeopathy, the vigorous shaking at each step of dilution.

remedy picture.say: In homeopathy, the full set of symptoms and traits a remedy matches.

potency.say: In homeopathy, how many times a remedy was diluted and shaken (6C, 30C, 200C).

GLP-1.say: A gut hormone; drugs that copy it (like semaglutide) lower blood sugar and appetite.

WADA.say: The World Anti-Doping Agency, which bans substances in sport.

haemochromatosis.say: An inherited condition where the body stores too much iron.

upper limit.say: The most you can take every day long-term without expecting harm, set by health agencies.

baraka.say: Blessing, a holy good fortune that can pass into things and people.

sanut.say: A word in a hadith on senna, read by scholars as honey, dill or cumin.

Bwiti.say: A religion of Gabon and its neighbours with iboga as its sacrament.

obi divination.say: Casting split kola lobes to answer a question.

zoopharmacognosy.say: The study of how animals use medicinal plants.

G6PD deficiency.say: An inherited enzyme shortage that makes red blood cells easy to break.

PPD.say: A black hair dye added to "black henna".

MAO.say: An enzyme that breaks down serotonin and other brain chemicals.

QT prolongation.say: A heart rhythm change that can lead to a dangerous arrhythmia.

CITES Appendix II.say: International trade allowed only with permits.

GRAS.say: "generally recognised as safe", a US food status.

inulin.say: A plant fibre that feeds gut bacteria.

medhya rasayana.say: A rasayana for the intellect and memory.

satva.say: A starch washed out of a crushed plant (guduchi).

shodhana.say: Purification of a raw drug or metal before use.

rasa shastra.say: Indian medical alchemy of metals and minerals.

varitara.say: The bhasma test: the ash must float on water.

madhumeha.say: "honey urine", the classical name for diabetes.

kampavata.say: The classical name for shaking (tremor) disorders.

mufarrih.say: A Unani "exhilarant" tonic for heart and spirits.

yuan qi.say: "original" qi, the energy a person is born with.

wei qi.say: The energy said to guard the skin against cold and wind like a screen.

invigorate the blood.say: Get stuck blood moving; stagnant blood is said to cause fixed, stabbing pain.

damp heat.say: Heat stuck with sticky fluid, e.g. in the gut or bladder.

clear heat and toxins.say: Cool the hot, red, swollen side of an illness.

sinking qi.say: The sense that energy is draining downward.

move the blood.say: In Chinese medicine, get stuck blood flowing.

sclerotium.say: A hard, compact mass of fungus.

nootropic.say: A supplement taken for memory and focus.

velada.say: The Mazatec all-night mushroom healing ceremony.

speleotherapy.say: Sessions spent breathing the air of salt mines or caves.

kurort.say: A Russian or Soviet spa resort.

argyria.say: Permanent blue-grey skin from swallowed silver.

rajata bhasma.say: Silver turned into a fine ash in Ayurvedic mineral medicine.

INR.say: The blood clotting test used with warfarin.

IUCN Red List.say: The world list of threatened species (Vulnerable, Endangered…).

pemmican.say: Dried meat, fat and berries pounded together.

escharotic salve.say: A paste that burns away flesh.

dieta.say: The strict diet kept around an ayahuasca ceremony.

icaros.say: Songs a healer sings in an ayahuasca ceremony.

k'intu.say: Three perfect coca leaves offered to the mountains.

cinchonism.say: Quinine poisoning: ringing ears, headache, nausea, blurred sight.

glochids.say: The fine hair-like spines of prickly pear.

catarrh.say: A blocked, runny nose or chest full of mucus.

furanocoumarins.say: Plant compounds that make skin burn in sunlight.

veno-occlusive disease.say: The small veins of the liver block up.

L-canavanine.say: An amino acid in alfalfa seeds and sprouts.

GLA.say: Gamma-linolenic acid, a fatty acid in borage and evening primrose oils.

prolactin.say: A hormone from the pituitary gland.

claudication.say: Leg pain on walking caused by narrowed arteries.

elf-shot.say: Sudden pains blamed on elves' invisible arrows (Anglo-Saxon).

EMA traditional use.say: The European Medicines Agency accepts a use based on long safe use, not trials.

well-established use.say: An EMA listing backed by clinical trials.

chronic venous insufficiency.say: Weak leg veins that let blood pool and ankles swell.

seborrhoeic skin.say: Greasy, flaky skin such as cradle cap.

Reye's syndrome.say: A rare brain and liver illness in children linked to aspirin.

thiaminase.say: An enzyme that breaks down vitamin B1.

moxa.say: Dried mugwort fluff burned over points on the skin.

anthroposophic medicine.say: A spiritual school of medicine founded in 1920s Switzerland.

ESCOP.say: A European herbal research group that writes plant monographs.

isoflavones.say: Plant compounds that act a little like oestrogen.

liver fire.say: In Chinese medicine, heat rising to the head (red eyes, headache).

trituration.say: Grinding an insoluble substance for hours with milk sugar before dilution.

constitutional remedy.say: One chosen for a person's lifelong type rather than a passing symptom.

polychrest.say: A remedy with a very wide range of use.

nosode.say: A remedy made from disease material.

vital force.say: The life energy that, in homeopathy, illness unsettles.

mucous membranes.say: The moist lining of the mouth, nose and gut.

counterirritant.say: A substance that cools or warms the skin to take the mind off pain.

cineole.say: The main compound of eucalyptus oil.

prepubertal gynaecomastia.say: Breast growth in boys before puberty.

aarti.say: The flame waved before a Hindu deity at the end of puja.

tilak.say: A devotional mark on the forehead.

khus tatti.say: Wetted vetiver-root screens hung in doorways.

CYP450.say: The liver enzymes that clear many drugs.

lipoid pneumonia.say: Lung inflammation from oil breathed into the lungs.

synephrine.say: The stimulant in bitter orange peel extract.

sevusevu.say: Fijian welcome ceremony where a visitor presents kava root to the chief.

kava dermopathy.say: Dry, scaly skin from heavy kava drinking.

canoe plants.say: Plants Polynesian voyagers carried between islands.

ʻinamona.say: Hawaiian relish of roasted kukui nut and salt.

smoking ceremony.say: Aboriginal cleansing rite with the smoke of burning leaves.

7-OH.say: 7-hydroxymitragynine, a strong opioid-acting compound in kratom, concentrated in some shop products.

oral submucous fibrosis.say: Stiffening of the mouth lining that can stop the mouth opening.

fu zi.say: Processed aconite side root in Chinese medicine.

rescue collapsed yang.say: Chinese medicine term, reviving the body's warm, active force when it fails.

alraun.say: German mandrake root doll kept for luck.

toloache.say: Datura used in Mexican and Californian Indigenous ceremonies.

Maha Shivaratri.say: Shiva's great night, a Hindu festival.

Walpurgis Night.say: The night of 30 April in European folklore.

pericarditis.say: Inflammation of the sac around the heart.

Category 2.say: FDA's list of compounding ingredients it says carry significant safety risks.

Category 1.say: Nominated ingredients FDA lets pharmacies use while it decides.

503A bulks list.say: The ingredients ordinary US pharmacies may legally compound from.

503B.say: Large outsourcing pharmacies that make compounded drugs in bulk.

enforcement discretion.say: A regulator saying it will not act against something that is still technically unlawful.

PCAC.say: FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee; its votes are advice, not law.

research use only.say: A label on vials meant to dodge drug law; FDA says it does not make human sale legal.

endotoxin.say: Fragments of dead bacteria that cause fever and shock when injected.

IGF-1.say: A growth factor the liver makes when growth hormone rises.

telomeres.say: Protective caps on the ends of chromosomes.

lipodystrophy.say: Fat building up or vanishing in the wrong places.

dysesthesia.say: Odd prickling or burning skin sensations.

NAION.say: A stroke of the optic nerve that can cost sight in one eye.

priapism.say: An erection lasting hours, an emergency.

dantian.say: The "elixir field" just below the navel where qi is gathered.

daoyin.say: Ancient Chinese stretching and breathing exercises.

breech.say: A baby lying bottom-first in the womb.

kundalini.say: Coiled energy at the base of the spine.

chakra.say: A wheel of energy along the spine.

löyly.say: The burst of steam from water on sauna stones.

kessa.say: A rough scrubbing glove used in the hammam.

temazcalero.say: The guide who leads a temazcal.

cold shock.say: The gasp and racing heart of the first minute in cold water.

hoʻoponopono.say: A Hawaiian family gathering to set things right.

attunement.say: The reiki rite that passes symbols to a student.

panema.say: In Panoan belief, bad luck and laziness.

refeeding syndrome.say: Dangerous shifts in the body when eating resumes after a very long fast.

mucilage herbs.say: Slimy, soothing plants such as marshmallow root, soaked cold.

unguentum.say: Latin for ointment, written on apothecaries' jars.

flying ointment.say: In witch lore, a salve rubbed on before the night flight to the sabbat.

lepa.say: A herbal paste spread on the skin.

oxymel.say: Honey and vinegar; sekanjabin is the Persian mint version.

spagyrics.say: Alchemical herbalism; spirit (alcohol), soul (essential oil) and body (salts) separated and rejoined.

solve et coagula.say: "dissolve and bind together", the alchemists' motto.

Semik and Trinity.say: Early-summer Slavic festivals about seven weeks after Easter.

rusalki.say: Water spirits of drowned maidens in Slavic belief.

ecdysterone.say: A steroid-like plant compound that insects use as a moulting hormone.

Buyan and Alatyr.say: The magic island and the holy stone at the centre of the world in Slavic charms.

vylivanie voska.say: Wax pouring, reading the shape of melted wax set in water.

koumissolechenie.say: A stay at a steppe sanatorium drinking koumiss (fermented mare's milk).

release the exterior.say: Chinese medicine, to bring on a sweat at the start of a cold.

warm the middle.say: Chinese medicine, to warm the stomach and spleen.

kidney yang.say: Chinese medicine, the body's deep store of heat.

functional dyspepsia.say: Indigestion with no clear cause found.

methaemoglobinaemia.say: A blood disorder that starves the body of oxygen.

EGCG.say: The main catechin in green tea, concentrated in extract pills.

L-theanine.say: A calming amino acid found in tea.

wind-heat.say: In Chinese medicine, a pattern of fever, headache and red eyes.

clear heat.say: In Chinese medicine, to cool an overheated body.

fluorosis.say: Damage to bones and teeth from too much fluoride.

pulegone.say: A liver toxin in some mints, including pennyroyal.

SCOBY.say: Symbiotic culture of bacteria and yeast, the disc that ferments kombucha.

acidosis.say: A dangerous build-up of acid in the blood.

protected designation of origin.say: An EU label that ties a food's name to its home region.

safe level.say: The highest intake EFSA is confident is safe when data are too thin for a formal upper limit.
